description: VeilChain rules: how fields, detected entities and labels map onto the classes of the organisation's policy. Where the policy does not list an example, the mapping below is a documented interpretation.

record_id.why: Surrogate key. It identifies no one outside the source system, but anyone holding the source file can link it back, so it is Internal rather than Public.

full_name.why: Policy lists customer records and employee contact details as Confidential.

email.why: Contact detail within a customer record (policy: Confidential).

phone.why: Contact detail within a customer record (policy: Confidential).

department.why: Organisational detail. Harmless alone, but a quasi-identifier: combined with other fields it can single out a person.

data_sensitivity.why: A label asserted by the data owner (low/medium/high). It is compared with the class VeilChain computes; it is not trusted blindly.

expected_redaction.why: Descriptive text about the expected result of a test case.

unknown_field.why: Default deny: a column the rules do not know about is treated as Confidential until someone classifies it.

entity_why.PERSON: Name of a data subject (customer record).
entity_why.EMAIL: Contact detail (customer record or employee contact detail).
entity_why.PHONE: Contact detail (customer record or employee contact detail).
entity_why.CARD: Payment card number. The policy does not list it, so it is treated as part of a customer record (Confidential). Design choice.
